page: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance belonging to the Famsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache per core. This instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression both placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also reaches the top tier at 17.89 GB/sec. Multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 decompression, fall into the average category. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only cached small blocks reaching 831.45 GB/sec and uncached large blocks reaching 53.49 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance achieves an average of 12.85 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks.

The F4ams_v7 instance offers a high-density memory profile relative to its 4 vCPUs, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial RAM without the overhead of additional CPU cores. However, a notable tradeoff is the lack of local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data. Additionally, while small-model LLM text generation performs in the top tier, prompt processing for larger 7B models is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and lightweight text generation tasks.
